name: 4.0 Twin-Turbo V8
notes: Variant: Audi RS 6 Avant (C8, 2019-2025 generation), base 4.0 TFSI 441 kW / 600 PS version as specified in Audi's eTD (Program for Germany, status 06/13/2024), with the standard 8-speed tiptronic (hydraulic torque converter with lock-up clutch) and quattro permanent all-wheel drive (mechanical centre differential, 40:60). The RS 6 Avant performance (463 kW, eTD status 10/08/2024) has identical gear ratios, final drive and base tyre size, so the gearbox data apply to it unchanged. Overall ratios = gear ratio x the single 3.204 final drive (the eTD lists no second final-drive stage): 4.714/3.143/2.106/1.667/1.285/1.000/0.839/0.667 x 3.204. Driven tyre: the base 275/35 R21 (same size on both axles; longitudinal quattro, so the rear axle is used); the optional 22-inch 285/30 R22 is 0.5 % larger in rolling circumference. Layout: 90-degree V8, 3,996 cc (86.0 x 86.0 mm), hot-V with one twin-scroll turbocharger per cylinder bank in the inside V (parallel twin-turbo). Firing order 1-3-7-2-6-5-4-8 per Audi's press kit and the EA825 self-study programme (not the 1-5-4-8-6-3-7-2 order of Ford-numbered V8s), at even 720/8 = 90-degree intervals. Audi numbering: cylinder bank 1 = right bank (in the direction of travel) = cylinders 1-4 = bank 0; cylinder bank 2 = left bank = cylinders 5-8 = bank 1 (SSP 920493: bank 1 right / bank 2 left; its cylinder-on-demand figure shows cylinder 1 at the front of the right bank, which carries the cylinder 2 and 3 cam actuators, with the cylinder 5 and 8 actuators on the left bank; injectors and ignition coils are grouped 1-4 / 5-8). Combustion entries in firing order give the bank pattern 0,0,1,0,1,1,0,1 (bank 0 fires at 0/90/270/540 deg, bank 1 at 180/360/450/630 deg): the uneven per-bank intervals (90/180/270/180) of a cross-plane crank, matching the SSP's statement that the firing order on each bank creates a 180-degree interval for some cylinders; with cylinders 2, 3, 5 and 8 deactivated (cylinder on demand) the remaining order 1-7-6-4 fires every 180 deg. The cross-plane crank is derived (first principles): Audi's documents state shared crankpins (opposite cylinders on one journal) and five main bearings but do not name the crank plane. EPA: the US Test Car List rows for this powertrain are screened out of the N/V check - MY2023 'RS6 Avant' (591 hp) and MY2024-2026 'RS 6 Avant' (621 hp, the performance): 8 gears, axle 3.2, N/V 25.0, whereas the test's rolling-circumference model gives 25.91 rpm/mph in 8th on 275/35R21 (+3.6 %; 25.78 on 285/30R22, +3.1 %). 25.0 equals 0.667 x 3.204 on the UNLOADED 285/30 R22 circumference (25.00), i.e. the filed N/V uses no rolling-radius reduction; the MY2021-2022 rows for the same powertrain filed as 'RS7' (591 hp, 8 gears, axle 3.2) give N/V 26.3 (model -1.5 %), so the filed values for one gear set and tyre size differ by 5 % and none is used. Sources disagree on the 441 kW compression ratio (10.1:1 in the 2023 press kit, 9.7:1 in the 2024 eTD; not used by the model). Estimated (not published by Audi in the documents used): redline and limiter 6,800 rpm, taken from Porsche's published maximum engine speed for its closely related 3,996 cc 86.0 x 86.0 mm V8 biturbo (Cayenne Turbo technical data, MY N, 04/2021) and above the 6,000-6,250 rpm band of Audi's rated 441 kW; limiter type fuel-soft with 150 rpm hysteresis; idle 650 rpm; shift time 0.20 s (torque-converter automatic default; Audi states only 'optimized shift times'); torque converter stallRpmWot 2,500 rpm, lockupTurbineRpm 1,200 rpm, couplingSR 0.90.
